title: The Days of Imprisonment
question: Today, can the narrator find any hope of escape from the Martian pit?
light: green firelight from below, black shadows

scullery_door.described: A dark Victorian scullery seen from the north-west corner beside the brick copper. Across grey York stone flags stands the planked kitchen door, half open, with a faint grey rectangle of light beyond it; a meat chopper with a wooden handle hangs on a nail beside the doorframe. At the left stand a brown stone sink and the dark silhouette of a cast-iron pump with a long curved handle; at the right two closed plank doors with iron latches. Walls of limewashed brick rise to a cracked ceiling of whitewashed boards. Grey light falls from the kitchen doorway at the far end across the flags toward the camera. Grey daylight through the doorway at the LEFT, deep shadow.
scullery_door.landmark: the planked kitchen door with the meat chopper on its nail
scullery_door.route: from the kitchen door across the flags to the pump and sink
scullery_door.geometry: The kitchen door stands at the far frame centre, a fifth of the frame's width, its grey rectangle the brightest area. The sink and pump fill the left frame edge near the camera at a sixth of the frame's width. The two plank doors fill the right frame edge. The flags run from the bottom frame edge up to the threshold of the kitchen door.
scullery_door.ambience: muffled clank of metal through the earth, plaster dust ticking down, held breath

pit_day.described: A small triangular hole in a ruined wall frames the view: a splintered beam crosses the top edge and broken bricks fill the bottom edge, with dark borders all around. Through it lies the far side of a vast pit of yellow clay and gravel, banked in terraces. A great opened metal cylinder lies at the centre, veils of bright green vapour drift above it, rods and plates lie in rows on a level shelf at the right, and a stack of white aluminium bars rises beside the shelf. On the far rim, among smashed shrubbery, a tall stiff three-legged machine stands against a warm blue sky. Gold light from the low sun falls from the right across the clay terraces.
pit_day.landmark: the opened metal cylinder at the centre of the pit
pit_day.route: from the splintered beam at the near edge across the pit floor to the cylinder at its centre
pit_day.geometry: The splintered beam crosses the top frame edge at a tenth of the frame's height. Broken bricks fill the bottom frame edge at a sixth of the frame's height. The opened cylinder lies at the frame centre, a quarter of the frame's width, with green vapour between it and the camera. The rods and plates run along the right frame edge on the level shelf, and the stack of bars rises at the right frame edge beside them. The three-legged machine stands at the far upper right, a tenth of the frame's height, on the rim.
pit_day.ambience: faint musical clinking of metal, a light wind over clay, the hiss of green vapour

scullery_copper.described: The north-west corner of a dim Victorian scullery. A brick-built wash copper rendered in limewash stands with a round wooden lid and a small iron fire door. A stack of split firewood leans beside it. A tall deal cupboard stands with its door ajar, showing dark wine bottles, tins of soup and salmon and two biscuit tins. Grey York stone flags run to the front edge of the picture, and limewashed brick walls rise behind. Faint grey light falls from the right, from the kitchen doorway, and lies along the flags. Low firelight from ahead, deep shadow.

scullery_copper.route: from the deal cupboard at the right along the flags to the copper at the corner
scullery_copper.geometry: The brick copper stands at the frame centre, a third of the frame's width, its round lid at the upper centre. The firewood stack leans at the left of the copper, a sixth of the frame's width. The deal cupboard stands at the right frame edge, a quarter of the frame's width, its door ajar toward the camera. Flags fill the bottom third of the frame.
scullery_copper.ambience: muffled clank of metal through the earth, dust ticking down, hushed breathing

scullery_dig.described: A wide interior of a dark Victorian scullery lit by grey daylight that falls in from the kitchen doorway behind the camera across the flags. The floor is stone-flagged and the walls are limewashed brick. At the right a shallow brown stone sink stands under a window blocked with earth, with a black cast-iron pump and its long curved handle beside it. In the far corner stand a brick-built wash copper with a round wooden lid and a stack of split firewood, and a tall deal cupboard. At the left two plank doors stand side by side with iron latches, the pantry door nearest the camera.

pit_night.described: A small triangular hole in a ruined wall frames the view, a splintered beam across its top edge and broken bricks along its bottom edge. The opened metal cylinder lies at the centre, a pale glowing machine stands at the foot of the near wall, bars of aluminium lie in bright patches, and a thin thread of green smoke rises at the right. A tall three-legged machine stands on the far bank against the sky. Pale light falls from the upper right across the clay terraces. Raking grey daylight from the LEFT, deep shadow.

shots.camera: Camera at chest height in front of the copper, a 85mm lens, looking at both men. The grey light comes from the RIGHT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the narrator's face at the LEFT, his head a third of the frame's height, his fist knotted in the curate's collar; the curate's face at the RIGHT, his head a third of the frame's height, hugging a biscuit tin; the copper's wooden lid behind them.
shots.end: The curate sags in the narrator's grip at the right, his cheek reddened, hands open, the biscuit tin on the flags at his feet; the narrator stands over him, fist lowered.

sounds.sound: a hard blow landing on a cheek, a gasp

source: I had, much as I loathed doing it, to resort to threats, and at last to blows.
shots.turn: the curate's carelessness -> the narrator's blows
shots.why: The narrator chooses threats and then blows to keep them both alive; it shows what he will do to keep the one chance of life.

shots.frame: Medium close on the curate (rather large pale blue eyes, black clerical waistcoat grey with plaster dust) sitting against the cupboard, one hand to his cheek, his eyes wide and wet.
shots.motion: The camera pushes in a hand's breadth across the whole shot toward the curate's face; his hand slides from his cheek to his mouth; tears run down his cheek.
shots.camera: Camera at floor height, a 85mm lens, looking at the curate. The grey light comes from the RIGHT.
shots.at_rest: THE FOCUS OF THE PICTURE IS the curate's face, his head a third of the frame's height, one hand pressed to his cheek; the deal cupboard door ajar behind his shoulder; the fallen biscuit tin on the flags at the lower RIGHT.
shots.end: The curate's face fills the frame, his hand over his mouth, pale blue eyes brimming, the dark cupboard behind him.
source: That brought him to reason for a time.
shots.turn: defiant carelessness -> cowed quiet
shots.why: The blow buys quiet at a price; it shows the narrator paying that price and owning it.

shots.frame: Wide from the kitchen doorway across the scullery: the narrator (grey eyes, cream flannel shirt with thin blue stripes) kneels at the left in the pantry doorway, the pantry door lifted off and leaning on the wall beside him, his hatchet biting into the earth.

source: It was on the third day, if my memory serves me right, that I saw the lad killed.
I went into the scullery, removed the door, and spent some hours digging with my hatchet as silently as possible
shots.turn: hope in digging -> a hole begun
shots.why: After the lad's death he tries to dig out; it shows the narrator acting alone while the curate lies broken.

source: That night was a beautiful serenity; save for one planet, the moon seemed to have the sky to herself.

shots.why: Picture only after the button: the machine works on under the moon, setting the narrator's new hope against an enemy still at its labour.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: A fighting-machine arrived, and fear drove us into the scullery.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: From that height, the Martian could see over our barrier.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Through the hole, I watched Martians make metal in the pit.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: A tentacle placed a bright bar on the stack.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: We fought for the chance to look, kicking and thrusting near danger.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Starvation waited, yet we fought over the peephole.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: He ate heavily and wept for hours, trusting his tears to save him.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I counted every tin that still remained.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: His muttering drove me close to craziness; I could not think.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: He was weak, fearful, and false even to himself.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: At dusk, the whole pit glowed green with aluminium fire.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The curate slid down; I took his place and watched.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: A tentacle reached into the cage and lifted a man against the stars.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Then hooting began; I ran into darkness.

lines.speaker: curate
lines.text: Do not leave me here! Come back, come back! I am alone in the dark with them near.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Next day, I took hold of myself and weighed our chances.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: They might leave, or forget to guard the pit.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Be quiet. One more sound, and I will strike you to keep us alive here in hiding together.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The blow quieted him; I am ashamed, yet I would strike again.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Those under such darkness may perhaps forgive me.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Days later, I watched a lad die before me.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I lifted the door and dug with my hatchet for hours.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Two feet down, the earth collapsed with a crash and stopped me.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I abandoned digging and lay on the flags.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Then came a booming: great guns, far off, and men were still fighting.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Six reports, then six more in reply.

lines.speaker: curate
lines.text: Guns. Those were guns. Someone still fights them out there.
